findings: Resisted trunk flexion/extension/side-flexion painless & strong
PA spring test normal/mild stiffness, no single hypermobile or rigid level
sttt.interpretation: Rules out a contractile lesion. Repeated movement assessment (McKenzie-style) is expected to show a directional preference.

cpa.pattern: "Inhibited, erector spinae dominant" is the textbook chronic-LBP CPA finding.

kineticChain.name: Lumbar Segmental Stability Tests
kineticChain.chainEffect: Used as a baseline (prone instability, ASLR, TA drawing-in) — expect normal or only mild TA drawing-in deficit, not a positive prone instability test.

functionalScreen.name: Sit-to-Stand
functionalScreen.note: The general hip-hinge-vs-lumbar-dominant strategy screen; a lumbar-dominant rise pattern here corroborates the TA/erector CPA finding.

L02.name: Lumbar Disc Herniation / Radiculopathy
recommended: Femoral nerve tension test (if upper lumbar)
specialTests: Femoral nerve tension test (if upper lumbar)

findings: Resisted hip/knee myotome tests (L4 quads, L5 EHL, S1 calf) may be weak & painless
Passive SLR/Slump reproduces leg pain
sttt.interpretation: Root involvement (not a contractile lesion) is supported — myotome weakness is painless (root pattern), and passive SLR/Slump reproduces neural, not capsular, pain.

muscles.name: Multifidus (at the herniated level)
muscles.state: Secondarily inhibited — recheck once acute phase settles

cpa.pattern: Not a classic muscle-pair pattern (neural compression). Recheck Multifidus at the herniated level once the acute phase settles — often secondarily inhibited.

kineticChain.name: Lumbar Flexion Control (Waiter's Bow)

fields.label: Forward bending pattern
options: Lateral trunk shift reducing on return

kineticChain.chainEffect: Watch for the "aberrant movement, painful arc" pattern — a lateral trunk shift on forward bending that reduces on return is explicitly documented as indicating disc herniation.

functionalScreen.name: Forward Bend (lateral shift + centralisation screen)
functionalScreen.note: The direct McKenzie-style functional correlate of this condition.

passive.label: PA spring test at the level

findings: Resisted trunk movements painless
Passive extension + rotation (Kemp's) reproduces local pain with a capsular end-feel
PA spring hypomobile/painful at the level
sttt.interpretation: Rules out a contractile lesion; capsular-pattern findings on passive extension/rotation localize the source to the facet joint.

cpa.pattern: "Inhibited, unilateral" classically co-occurs with segmental facet irritation.

kineticChain.name: Lumbar Rotation Control
kineticChain.chainEffect: A stiff thoracic spine forcing lumbar load-bearing rotation can drive facet loading — check thoracic rotation before treating the facet in isolation.

functionalScreen.name: Squat Pattern
functionalScreen.note: Watch the return-to-stand (extension) phase specifically, since facet loading is most provoked there.

findings: Resisted tests generally painless (non-contractile)
Passive extension reproduces leg symptoms (canal narrows)
Flexion relieves — the inverse of a typical disc pattern
sttt.interpretation: Bicycle test / stoop test and treadmill testing (neurogenic vs vascular claudication) are the key provocative maneuvers for distinguishing stenosis from a disc pattern.

muscles.name: TA / Multifidus
muscles.state: Often globally inhibited from long-standing guarding

muscles.name: Glute Max
muscles.state: Frequently also inhibited from reduced walking tolerance (deconditioning)

cpa.pattern: Global inhibition pattern from long-standing guarding and deconditioning.

kineticChain.name: Lumbar Flexion Control
kineticChain.chainEffect: Expect the inverse of the disc pattern: flexion-biased postures relieve, extension provokes; a McKenzie flexion preference here fits stenosis rather than herniation.

functionalScreen.name: Squat Pattern
functionalScreen.note: Assess tolerance for a flexion-biased loading strategy, since gait-based bicycle/stoop provocation (STTT above) isn't part of this app's seated/standing functional screen set.

L05.name: Sacroiliac Joint (SIJ) Dysfunction
required: SIJ provocation CLUSTER: Compression, Distraction, Sacral Thrust, Gaenslen's, FABERE/Patrick, Gillet's
recommended: Palpation (PSIS, sacral sulcus — weak inter-rater reliability)
ESR/CRP/HLA-B27 referral if inflammatory features co-exist

findings: Resisted hip abduction/extension may be painful secondarily (glute med/involved musculature)
The SIJ provocation cluster is the primary joint-play equivalent
sttt.interpretation: SIJ provocation cluster: 3+ of 5 positive = SIJ source; active SLR is also part of the required battery. (Note: the source lists six named sub-tests under "cluster" — Compression, Distraction, Sacral Thrust, Gaenslen's, FABERE/Patrick, Gillet's — while its own scoring rule refers to "3+ of 5"; both are reproduced verbatim here.)

cpa.pattern: "Inhibited, QL dominant" is the classic driver of SIJ-pattern pain via altered force closure.

kineticChain.name: Lumbar Segmental Stability's Active Straight Leg Raise component
kineticChain.chainEffect: Manual ASIS compression improving the ASLR is the direct documented sign of an SIJ force-closure deficit.

functionalScreen.name: Single Leg Stance (SIJ & Lumbopelvic Control / Trendelenburg)
functionalScreen.note: The named functional test for exactly this pattern.

L06.name: Lumbar Instability
required: Observation for instability jog during active movement
observation: Instability jog / catch during active movement
posture: Excessive segmental motion on PA spring

findings: Resisted trunk tests may be strong but poorly controlled (an instability "catch" on active movement, not true weakness)
Passive PA spring shows a hypermobile segment
sttt.interpretation: Prone instability test and H & I stability tests are the primary provocative maneuvers for this condition.

cpa.pattern: "Inhibited, bilateral" with erector-spinae global substitution is the textbook instability CPA pattern.

kineticChain.name: Lumbar Segmental Stability Tests

fields.label: Prone instability test / ASLR / abdominal drawing-in

kineticChain.chainEffect: The direct match: prone instability test, ASLR, and abdominal drawing-in are this app's own instability battery.

functionalScreen.name: Rotary Stability (FMS) + Trunk Stability Push-Up (FMS)
functionalScreen.note: The two generic core-stability screens most directly relevant to a diagnosed instability.

L07.name: Spondylolisthesis / Spondylolysis
recommended: SPECT/MRI if x-ray negative but suspicion high
Meyerding grading once imaging confirms slip

resisted.label: Resisted trunk extension
options: Reproduces pain at the pars/slip level

findings: Resisted trunk extension reproduces pain at the pars/slip level (the Stork test is this same single-leg extension provocation)
Passive extension is often the most provocative movement
sttt.interpretation: Stork test (single-leg hyperextension) reproducing pain is the key provocative finding for this condition.

muscles.name: TA + Multifidus (segmental stabilisers, at the slip level)
muscles.state: Assess as for Lumbar Instability's core-stability logic

cpa.pattern: Same core-stability logic as Lumbar Instability (L06), since dynamic segmental control limits further slip.

kineticChain.name: Lumbar Segmental Stability Tests + Lumbar Flexion Control

fields.label: Prone instability test at the slip level

kineticChain.chainEffect: The prone instability test at the slip level, plus watching for extension-provoked pain (the stork-test principle applied functionally).

functionalScreen.name: Sit-to-Stand / Squat Pattern
functionalScreen.note: Note any pain specifically on the extension/return phase, mirroring the Stork test's single-leg hyperextension provocation.

L08.name: Lumbar Muscle Strain
recommended: X-ray only if red flags present
observation: Visible muscle spasm / guarding on movement
posture: Antalgic lean away from strained side

resisted.label: Resisted trunk movement in the direction of strain

passive.label: Passive stretch of the same muscle

findings: Resisted trunk movement in the direction of strain is strong but painful (classic Cyriax contractile-lesion pattern)
Passive stretch of the same muscle is also painful
sttt.interpretation: Resisted isometric movements reproduce pain — per Cyriax classification, strong + painful = contractile lesion.

muscles.name: Erector Spinae or QL (whichever strained)
muscles.state: Check whether primary strain or an overactive compensator (2° to TA/glute max inhibition)

cpa.pattern: Check whether it's a primary strain or an OVERACTIVE COMPENSATOR before treating as isolated.

kineticChain.name: Lumbar Flexion Control
kineticChain.chainEffect: Expect a guarded, direction-specific restriction (pain-limited, not a true motor-control fault); reassess as the strain settles.

functionalScreen.name: Sit-to-Stand
functionalScreen.note: Document the guarded rise strategy at baseline to track recovery of a normal hip-hinge pattern.

L09.name: Lumbar Myofascial Pain
required: Palpation for taut bands/trigger points reproducing referred pain
palpation: Taut bands/trigger points reproducing referred pain
Myofascial trigger point / taut band network

resisted.label: Resisted test of muscle under trigger-point suspicion
options: Reproduces referred (not true) pain, no true weakness

findings: Resisted tests reproduce referred (not true) pain from the palpated trigger point, no true weakness
sttt.interpretation: Palpation reproducing the referred pain pattern is the key finding for this condition.

cpa.pattern: This is very often the SYMPTOM of a deeper glute-inhibition pattern, not a primary muscle problem.

kineticChain.reason: Not primarily a joint-mobility condition (myofascial referral) — the Single Leg Stance / hip-focused screens are more informative than a lumbar mobility test.

functionalScreen.name: Sit-to-Stand / Forward Bend
functionalScreen.note: Check whether a lumbar-flexion-dominant strategy is loading these exact muscles, consistent with the CPA finding above.

L10.name: Inflammatory Back Pain (Axial Spondyloarthritis Pattern)
required: Lumbar AROM all planes (uniform vs single-plane restriction)
specialTests: FABER Test (+ posterior SIJ provocation — cross-refer L05)

findings: Resisted tests generally painless early (inflammatory, not mechanical)
Passive ROM uniformly restricted, non-capsular
sttt.interpretation: AROM uniformly restricted in all planes (non-capsular pattern) is the defining functional finding for this condition.

cpa.reason: Not applicable — systemic inflammatory diagnosis, not a motor-control compensation pattern.

kineticChain.name: Lumbar Flexion Control + Rotation Control
kineticChain.chainEffect: Expect GLOBAL, non-directional restriction rather than the directional preference seen in L01–L09.

functionalScreen.name: Sit-to-Stand + Forward Bend
functionalScreen.note: Both should show symmetric, globally reduced range rather than a specific direction of preference.

L11.name: Serious Pathology / Red Flag
L11.body: Cauda equina indicator → EMERGENCY same-day referral. Fracture, inflammatory, or other serious-pathology red flag → URGENT referral before continuing.
L11.action: Replaces the differential list entirely when triggered. No module cards or test suggestions render. STTT/CPA: not applicable — do not resisted-test or compensation-test until the red flag is cleared.
